status: RECONCILED - now SPENT as a validator (used to find and fix the zone defect)
purpose: Out-of-sample validation. harbor-eb-60s was used to FIND and FIX a defect, so it can no longer validate the method (lessons.md L-007). This is a different 60s window the method has never been tuned against.

source.camera: SR-90 at Harbor Blvd, CCTV 506, Caltrans D12 (SAME camera as benchmark A)

definition.what_is_counted: A vehicle whose body crosses the vertical line x=600 within y=[300,680], travelling LEFT to RIGHT (eastbound approach volume: left-turns AND throughs together).

method_under_test.description: YOLO11n + ByteTrack -> tripwire crossing, direction from LOCAL motion at the crossing, counted only if within 30 degrees of perpendicular to the line.
method_under_test.no_tuning_permitted: The threshold and all parameters were fixed on benchmark A BEFORE this window was cut. Changing anything after seeing the user's count would void this as an out-of-sample test.

sealed_prediction.sealed_at: 2026-10-02, BEFORE any human count of this window
sealed_prediction.detail: see benchmarks/harbor-eb-60s-B/sealed_prediction.json for per-crossing times and angles

user.count_type: REVIEWED (revised from a blind 13 after watching QA2_review.mp4)
user.provenance: Blind count was 13. On review with the numbered overlay the user found TWO vehicles their own blind count had also missed, revising to 14.

caveats: SAME camera and SAME day as benchmark A - this is a different-window test, not a different-site test. It controls for traffic but not for camera geometry or lighting.
A genuinely independent test needs a DIFFERENT CAMERA (Beach or Brea Blvd are on disk) and ideally a WEEKDAY, where queues and congestion are present.

result.note: The ORIGINAL out-of-sample figure of 92.3% was computed against the user BLIND count of 13. The reference is now 14, so the honest blind out-of-sample result is 85.7%.

sample_size_limitation: CRITICAL: with 13 vehicles, ONE error = 7.7%. The benchmark therefore cannot resolve stage 2 (92.75%) from stage 3 (98%) - the only reachable scores near the top are 92.3% (one error) and 100% (zero errors), with nothing in between. To measure 98% meaningfully one error must be <2%, requiring N>=50 vehicles. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE LADDER: the 1-minute unit is adequate for stage 1 but CANNOT validate stage 3. Later rungs need longer windows or busier periods.

error_analysis.user_words: "when you counted seven, there is a car which goes under it, which got missed... at 00:56 a dark grey sedan is missed and the next truck is counted. so its total of 14"

miss_1.cause: ZONE DEFINITION - crossed at y=689, outside the hand-drawn band y=[300,680]. The tripwire stopped mid-roadway.

miss_2.vehicle: dark blue car below the white SUV
miss_2.cause: NOT a detection miss (L-010 was wrong). All 18 model configurations tested - yolo11n/s/m at imgsz 960/1280/1920, conf 0.15/0.05 - DETECTED it. Track 6371 was first observed at x=602.4, past the x=600 tripwire. A track born downstream of the line can never cross it.
miss_2.fix: Place the tripwire where tracks are mature, downstream of the track-birth region.

error_analysis.fix_applied: Extend the tripwire to span the full roadway (y=300-720). Principled: the line visibly terminated mid-road.

after_fix.regression_check: A unchanged at 20 - the fix does not trade one benchmark against the other.

error_analysis.adr_prediction_wrong: ADR-0001 predicted occlusion would dominate the error budget once fragmentation was removed. It did not. The dominant error was ZONE DEFINITION - a hand-drawn tripwire that did not span the roadway. Only one of two errors was occlusion-adjacent.
